name: Identify common cloud formations
blurb: Ten cloud types, sorted by height and shape, let you read the next several hours of weather off the sky — a genuinely useful skill for anyone who goes outdoors.
gear: A phone camera for a personal reference album
steps: Learn the three altitude families: cirro- (high, icy), alto- (middle), and low cloud, plus the vertically developed ones.
Learn the shape words: cumulus is heaped, stratus is layered, nimbus means rain-bearing, cirrus is wispy.
Combine them: cirrostratus, altocumulus, stratocumulus, nimbostratus, cumulonimbus.
Learn the classic warm-front sequence — cirrus, then cirrostratus, then altostratus, then rain — which gives 12 to 24 hours of warning.
Learn the towering cumulus to cumulonimbus progression that means a thunderstorm within hours.
Photograph the sky daily for a fortnight, name each type, and note what the weather actually did.
tips: Height and shape, in that order. Getting the family right narrows it to two or three options immediately.
A halo around the sun or moon means high ice cloud, which often means rain in a day.
proof: You name the cloud types overhead and correctly predict the next few hours, several days running.
